03 · Correction

Machine polishing & paint correction

Machine polishing removes a very thin layer of clear coat to level out swirl marks, haze and light scratches, so the paint reflects light evenly again.

What polishing can improve

  • Swirl marks, often caused by washing with dirty mitts, brushes or automatic car washes
  • Haze and dullness
  • Light scratches that sit within the clear coat
  • Marks left by previous poor polishing (holograms)
  • Light water-spot marks

What it can't fix

  • Scratches that have gone through to the colour coat or primer
  • Stone chips
  • Dents
  • Peeling or failed lacquer

These need paint repair, not polishing.

Enhancement or correction?

A one-stage polish (often called an enhancement) improves gloss and removes a good share of light defects in a day.

A multi-stage correction uses a cutting stage followed by a finishing stage. It removes more, takes longer and suits paint with heavier swirls.

How the job is done

[CONFIRM WITH REBEL: Rebel's actual process. Typical steps are listed below. Edit them to match what Connor does.]

  1. Wash A full pre-wash, snow foam and hand wash.
  2. Decontaminate Iron fallout and tar removed, then the paint clayed so it's smooth.
  3. Inspect The paint is checked under strong light to see what needs correcting.
  4. Mask Trim, rubbers and edges are taped to protect them.
  5. Polish Panel by panel, checking progress as it goes.
  6. Protect Freshly polished paint is protected, with a sealant or a ceramic coating.

Machine polishing questions

Will polishing remove every scratch?

No. It removes or reduces defects that sit within the clear coat. Scratches through to the colour coat or primer, and stone chips, need paint repair. We'll tell you what to expect before starting.

Does polishing harm the paint?

It removes a very thin layer of clear coat, which is how it levels out defects. That's why it's done carefully and not repeated often. Afterwards, protecting the paint and washing it safely keeps the result for longer.
